title: batchMint lacks nonReentrant; ERC1155 onERC1155Received callback fires mid-loop
description: BatchNFTMinter does not inherit ReentrancyGuard (unlike sibling NFTStaker). ERC1155 _mint invokes onERC1155Received on the caller-chosen recipient mid-loop (per iteration, before forceApprove(0) and the nudge payout) while max approval is live, paymentAmount is held, and the nudge pot is intact. Re-examined this run (phoenix-nft-staking-14) with a decisive, validated Tier-3 PoC.
impact: Defensive gap only. The missing nonReentrant guard is real, but the High escalation (third-party fund theft) is NOT supported. The clean reentrancy theft of an honest multi-mint caller's in-flight funds atomically reverts: the nested frame's forceApprove(minter, 0) at L261 revokes the outer loop's live approval, so the re-entrant mint cannot draw against the honest caller's held budget. The only value-moving reentrancy paths require honest-caller misconfiguration (over-fund the call AND designate the attacker as recipient = known-invalid user mistake). The donated-paymentToken sweep is documented intended behavior with an owner rescueERC20 hatch. Becomes HIGH only if the payout were changed to fixed-amount or a per-caller balance were retained.
attackPath: 1. Reentrancy is reachable (recipient onERC1155Received callback fires mid-loop) while approval/budget/pot are live.

2. Clean third-party theft path: nested frame attempts to drain the outer caller's in-flight funds, but forceApprove(minter, 0) at L261 in the nested frame revokes the outer loop's approval => the outer continuation reverts atomically, no theft.

3. Remaining value-moving paths require honest-caller misconfiguration (over-fund + attacker as recipient) => out-of-scope user mistake; or rely on the donated-token sweep which is intended behavior with an owner rescue hatch.
Net: defensive gap / parity issue only; becomes High only under speculative future changes (fixed-amount payout or retained per-caller balance).
recommendation: Add OZ ReentrancyGuard and apply nonReentrant to batchMint for parity with the sibling NFTStaker and defense-in-depth against future payout changes. Additionally, make the refund credit a recorded/tracked amount rather than balanceOf(this), so future payout-shape changes cannot reopen a reentrancy value-extraction path.

poc.note: 4 cases, all pass against real source @ 9be4a87. Demonstrates: (a) clean third-party theft attempt reverts atomically via nested forceApprove(0); (b) value-moving paths only via honest-caller misconfiguration; (c) donated-token sweep is intended; (d) reentrancy is reachable but non-extractable.

metadata.verdict: STAYS LOW. High escalation (third-party fund theft) refuted by validated Tier-3 PoC @ 9be4a87.
